[NFCT.1.1] A schema reaches the engine from a compiled artefact, and in no
other way: `ds_engine_load_dsc` registers every schema (and rule) the `.ds`
source declared, with the schemas of the built-in module ([LIMP.12.2]). A fact
type an adapter supplies is declared in the program, as an `ambient` schema
where rules only read it ([LADP.2.1.1]). See [NGST.4].

**Registration is setup-phase only.** Every schema an engine holds must be
registered before the engine emits its first stream event, and the engine must
refuse a load after that with `DS_ERR_STATE`. A host
assert, a retract and a pump each emit one, so registration comes before the
first of them; loading an artefact and seeding the cache ([NLFC.9.1]) emit none.
The schema set is therefore fixed before anything on the stream can name a
schema, which is what lets an encoder announce all of it at the head of a
stream ([RFCS.5.1]).

A single `.dsc` load is everything assert
needs — the engine builds its own
matching working-memory and Rete state internally.

**An engine holds one artefact.** After a
successful `ds_engine_load_dsc`, the engine must refuse a second load, of the
same artefact or of another, with `DS_ERR_STATE`, and leave its state
unchanged. A recording's header names one rule set by its hash ([LFST.4.7]),
and a replay loads that one artefact ([RFCS.4.5]), so an engine holding two
would run a program no recording describes. A load that failed spent the engine
([RDSC.9.8]), so that engine takes no other load.
